nodes.label: Patient presented with three weeks of jaundice
A 71-year-old man also reported weight loss, abdominal pain, and dark-colored urine over the same three-week period
Patient reported bilateral lower-extremity weakness most noticeable when arising from a chair, resulting in several ground-level falls, with no prolonged periods of being down
Patient had no history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions and takes atorvastatin as a home medication
Physical examination showed significant scleral icterus, epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound, and mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles
CT shows a 2.6×3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with pancreatic ductal dilatation
CA19-9 is markedly elevated at 2930 with bilirubin 169.3 and ALP 894
Markedly elevated CK and renal decline are present
Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma causing malignant biliary obstruction
Proximal lower-extremity weakness is speculated to be a paraneoplastic myopathy associated with pancreatic head adenocarcinoma
